headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 7 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: The first summit finish of La Vuelta 26! The riders already had an uphill rendezvous in Font-Romeu (stage 3) but extreme weather flipped the script. Today, the sky seems much more clement, as the riders head to Aramon Valdelinares with 149.8 km of racing (3,685 metres of elevation). The neutral start is set at 13:35 in Vall d’Alba, the start proper at 13:40 after a 1.7 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Cycling history in Vall d’Alba
subtext: Vall d’Alba is a La Vuelta stage town for the first time*. Vall d’Alba was the setting of the time trials at the 2018 Spanish national championships. Jonathan Castroviejo won the men’s elite title and Mavi Garcia the women’s elite title. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: Pogacar made it 3 already at La Vuelta 26, and 38 in total in Grand Tours
subtext: Yesterday, Tadej Pogacar became the first rider with three stage wins in the first six days of La Vuelta since Oscar Freire in 2007. With a 38th Grand Tour stage win (26 in the Tour, 6 in La Vuelta, 6 in the Giro), he passed Rik Van Looy (37) as the 9th all time best scorer. Delio Rodriguez and Learco Guerra are tied at 7th place with 39 wins each. The former took all these victories in La Vuelta: 12 in 1941, 8 in 1942, 6 in 1945, 5 in 1946 and8 in 1947.

headline: Mas joined the list of runner-ups to Pogacar
subtext: Although Enrica Mas was 2nd to Tadej Pogacar at Il Lombardia 2022 (a week after beating him at the Giro dell’Emilia) and in stages 2 and 4 of the Vuelta a Andalucia 2023, yesterday was the first time they finished 1st and 2nd in a Grand Tour stage. It makes Mas the 20th rider to finish second to Pogacar in a Grand Tour stage. Ethan Hayter and Jarno Widar also joined that list during La Vuelta 26: 14 times - Jonas Vingegaard 3 - Primoz Roglic 2 - Remco Evenepoel, Dani Martinez, Nairo Quintana 1 - Tom Dumoulin, Felix Gall, Filippo Ganna, Ethan Hayter, Matteo Jorgenson, Stefan Küng, Lenny Martinez, Michael Matthews, Enric Mas, Valentin Paret-Peintre, Giulio Pellizzari, Isaac del Toro, Alejandro Valverde, Mathieu Van der Poel, Jarno Widar

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 1.7 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: With another stage win, Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) is more than ever the overall leader of La Vuelta 26. Enric Mas (Movistar) was the only one able to accompany him to Castello and he is now second (+3’34’’). He had not been so high in the GC of a Grand Tour since stage 5 of La Vuelta 23 (2nd to Remco Evenepoel), also raced in the province of Castello. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is now third with a gap of 4’21’’. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) and Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) are the other two riders within five minutes of Pogacar (4’50’’ and 4’55’’) respectively.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Leader of the points standings since his opening victory in Monaco, Tadej Pogacar is now up to 102 points. Since he wears La Roja, it will be Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) racing with the green jersey. The Belgian all-rounder won yesterday’s intermediate sprint to bring his tally up to 69 points. His teammate Matthew Brennan is third with 60 points.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) took 11 KOM points over the first summit of the day, and Enric Mas went first at Puerto El Bartolo, but Tadej Pogacar also retains the lead of the mountains standings (29 points). Mas will be racing with the polka-dot jersey today as he is second in the standings ahead of Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana): 14 points for the Spaniard, 13 for the Italian climber.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Struggling on the final part of the Puerto El Bartolo ascent, Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) dropped to the 7th place in the overall standings (+5’37’’) and very narrowly retained the white jersey as the leader of the young riders standings. Breakaway rider Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) is only 3 seconds behind. Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) lost time and now trails by 2’31’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Felix Gall (6th), Matthew Riccitello (23rd) and Gregor Mühlberger (25th), Decathlon CMA CGM had the best collective performance yesterday and took the lead of the team standings ahead of UAE Emirates XRG (+4’22’’) and Netcompany Ineos (+16’01’’).

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) will once again race with a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider for the second time (stages 4 and 6).

headline: Stage 7 is ON!
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) immediately attacks.

headline: 3 attackers: Van Aert, Vader, Leknessund
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) accelerated as soon as the flag dropped. Milan Vader (Bahrain Victorious) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) are with them. The peloton trail by 27'' at km 3.

headline: 4 chasers
subtext: Paul Ourselin (Cofidis), Hannes Wilksch (Tudor), Timo Roosen (Picnic PostNL) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) try to join the lead trio.

headline: The gap significantly increases
subtext: The lead trio are already at km 9. The four chasers trail by 1'. New counter-attackers set off from the b unch, already two minutes behind the leaders.

headline: Wout van Aert, Milan Vader and Andreas Leknessund
XDS Astana react
subtext: Alessandro Romele sets a strong pace and the gap from the lead trio to the bunch drops down to 1'35''. The chasers are just ahead.

headline: The chasers are caught by the bunch at km 16
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Milan Vader (Bahrain Victorious) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) are 1'20'' ahead.

headline: 2 leaders: Van Aert and Leknessund
subtext: Vader is dropped from the breakaway at km 19.

headline: 20 kilometres of battle
subtext: Many riders try to counter-attack a minute behind the lead duo. We've just seen Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH) try to get away. Today is quite a special day for the Spaniard...

headline: Herrada on the move on "home roads"?
subtext: Many Spanish riders (as well as Colombia’s Sergio Higuita) are used to training in the area, part of the Sierra de Gudar, next to the Sierra de Javalambre. It’s the case of Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH), who is set to retire at the end of La Vuelta 26. Today’s course echoes the first of his three La Vuelta victories, in 2019: the stage started in Mora de Rubielos (km 122 on today’s course) and finished in Ares del Maestrat (around 40 kilometres north of today’s start). “To be honest, it’s a marvellous place", the Spanish vetera said at the start. "My brother José and I started coming here quite a few years ago to train, and I really loved it for training. It’s at 1,700 metres, in Spain’s highest village, and it’s practically been my second home for many years – I’ve held all my training camps there over the years. Because of the quality of the place, the people… everything. I wouldn’t change it for anything. The finish is very tough. The stage is short, but it involves a lot of elevation gain, constantly climbing with passes of 6–7 kilometres. And above all, the final climb has some very steep sections, at over 10%. The finish is at almost 2,000 metres. We’re hoping a breakaway can make it through and that we can be right there.”

headline: 3 new chasers: Lutsenko, Bisiaux, Zana
subtext: Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) and Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) already attacked together yesterday. They are joined by Italy's Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step). More attackers try to ge in the mix.

subtext: With under 5 kilometres to the summit, they are 35'' behind the leaders.

headline: 3 more attackers set off from the bunch
subtext: Sergio Samitier (Cofidis), Juan Felipe Rodríguez (EF Education-EasyPost) and Mats Wenzel (Equipo Kern Pharma) are 2 minutes behind the lead duo and 15 seconds ahead ot he peloton.

headline: 5 leaders into the last kilometre of ascent
subtext: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) and Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) join Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) at the front. The first chasers trial by 40 seconds, and the peloton by 2'30''.

headline: Samitier, Rodriguez and Wenzel join the chase group
subtext: That makes 22 riders 50 seconds behind the five leaders, who are at the bottom of the second climb of the day, the cat. 3 Alto de Zucaina.

headline: Leknessund leads the way to the summit
subtext: Results at Alto de Zucaina (cat. 3, km 65.5): 1. Leknessund, 3 pts 2. Johannessen, 2 pts 3. Van Aert, 1 pt The gap to the chasers is up to 1'25'', and 3'30'' to the peloton.

headline: Samitier: "The three of us from Aragon would love to be in the breakaway"
subtext: Sergio Samitier (Cofidis) is one of three Aragonese riders headed for a home finish, along with Pablo Castrillo and Jorge Arcas. And he made the breakaway, just like he hoped for at the start: "This year’s Vuelta is centred on southern Spain, but we do touch on Aragon a little, so it’s always a thrill for the three of us from Aragon [along with Jorge Arcas and Pablo Castrillo] who are competing in La Vuelta a España. The three of us from Aragon would love to be in the breakaway and for Pogacar to let this breakaway go through so we can contest the race. It’s very difficult because, in the end, everyone will want to be there, but we’re going to fight for it. For now, we’ve got the desire, the attitude and the strength… for now!"

headline: Halfway through the stage
subtext: The five leaders enter the second half of the stage (75 km to go) with a gap of 1'20'' to the chase group. The peloton trail by 3'40''.

headline: Warbasse (kind of) knows today's challenges
subtext: Larry Warbasse (Tudor) is one of five La Vuelta 26 riders who climbed Aramon Valdelinares in 2014. Now he's in the breakaway alongside Marco Brenner. Just this morning, on the bus right here, I was checking to see the last time they did it in the Vuelta, and it was 2014, and that was my first Vuelta", Warbasse said at the start. "I was like ‘oh wow, I guess I’ve done the climb before’. I went and rewatched it, and I can’t say I remember anything! The bikes have improved a lot since then. It’s pretty crazy. Everything has changed you know. Disc brakes are probably number 1, and then everything is more aerodynamic; now we’re on tubeless tyres instead of tubulars, so there’s been really a lot of changes. It hasn’t gotten any easier, that’s for sure! You can go faster, but it’s still at least as hard if not harder than before, for sure.”

headline: Vine: "If you ask anyone in the peloton if they’d like to win again, I think they’d say yes"
subtext: La Vuelta 26 is Jay Vine’s first Grand Tour with Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG): “It’s a really nice experience. Helping him win the race is one of my goals, to be part of a Grand Tour winning team, so it’s pretty incredible. If you ask anyone in the peloton if they’d like to win again, I think they’d say yes, but every day is a new day and we’re only on stage 7, so we’ll see how it goes. Personally, I’m really looking forward to Montreal and the TT there. So coming out of this Vuelta like I did last year with some good legs for the end of the season would be nice.”

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 42.6 km/h
subtext: The five leaders are about to enter the final 60 kilometres. +1'40'' Chase group +3'55'' Peloton

headline: Bad cooperation in the chase group
subtext: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) tried to split the chase group but he's reeled in. They are 1'45'' behind the five leaders.

headline: Will the breakaway make it today?
Johannessen and Leknessund to make it a special day for Norway?
subtext: Today at the start, the Norwegian riders in La Vuelta 26 came to the front line as a minute of silence was observed after their king Harald V passed away. "It is of course very sad for all Norwegians", their compatriot Embret Svestad-Bardseng (Netcompanys Ineos) said. "He’s been sick not for a while, but for a week or so, and when you get the news that he’s passed away it’s of course very sad. He was a role model for all the citizens. He was a good man. He was also really sports invested. He really liked and enjoyed to watch sports like ski, football, whatever. A great person has passed away and we’re all sad in Norway today.”

headline: The road rises again
subtext: The ascent of the Puerto de Fuente de Rubielos (5.9km at 6.3%) markes the entrance into the final 50 kilometres of the stage. The chasers still trail by a minute and a half. Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious) increases the pace. The gap to the peloton is up to almost 5 minutes.

headline: The chasers move closer on the ascent
subtext: Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious) and Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) are particularly active to bring the gap down to 1'10''.

headline: Results at Puerto de Fuente de Rubielos (cat. 3, km 104.9)
subtext: 1. Van Aert, 3 pts 2. Lutsenko, 2 pts 3. Dunbar, 1 pt

headline: Dunbar: "It's like a game of chess"
subtext: At the start, Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5)discussed the right conditions for a break to make it to the finish: “I thought yesterday would be more suited to a breakaway than today… I actually don’t know. I think half the peloton are hoping to break. It just depends how long takes to go. If it takes 40, 50, 60 k to go, I think it could end up being a GC day. But who knows? You just need the right combination. I think if every team was able just to get a rider in they’d be quite happy. But it doesn’t quite work like that. Some teams always want two riders, some teams maybe try to get as many riders as they can. It’s like a game of chess. The right move goes in a random moment and you just hope that you’re in it.”

headline: The 3rd La Vuelta finish at Aramon Valdelinares
subtext: Aramon Valdelinares has hosted two La Vuelta stage finishes. In 2005, Roberto Heras took the stage and the overall lead. In 2014, two Colombians shared the glory: Winner Anacona won the stage ahead of Alexey Lutsenko, and Nairo Quintana took La Roja for the first time in his career. On both occasions, Puerto de San Rafael was the penultimate climb of the day, just before the final ascent, just like today. The climb to Aramon Valdelinares was also a classic of the former Vuelta a Aragon.

headline: 5 La Vuelta 26 riders were already at Aramon Valdelinares in 2014
subtext: - Alexey Lutsenko, 2nd of the stage - Pello Bilbao, 5th - Mikel Landa, 49th - Larry Warbasse, 93rd - George Bennett, 101st For both Lutsenko and Bilbao, it was their first top 10 result in a Grand Tour. Bilbao and Warbasse were doing their first Grand Tour.

headline: 35 kilometres to go
subtext: The five leaders are headed for the intermediate sprint (26.5 km to go). The gap to the chasers is stable: 1'15''. The gap to the bunch is up to 5'50''.

headline: The peloton keep losing time (6'30'')
subtext: Into the final 30 kilometres, it's pretty clear the stage win is either for one of the five leaders or one of their chasers.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Van Aert wins the intermediate sprint
subtext: The Belgian star now has 89 points. Pogacar still leads the standings with 102 points.

headline: Results of the intermediate sprint (km 122.3)
subtext: 1. Van Aert, 20 pts / 6'' 2. Lutsenko, 17 pts / 4'' 3. Dunbar, 15 pts / 2'' 4. Johannessen, 13 pts 5. Leknessund, 10 pts

headline: Onto the penultimate climb of the day
subtext: The five leaders tackle the climb of the Puerto de San Rafael (11.1km at 4.3%) with a lead up to a minute and a half.

headline: Van Boven suffers a hard tumble
subtext: Luca Van Boven (Lotto Intermarché) goes down after an unfortunate move by an XDS Astana rider.

headline: The leaders still collaborate
subtext: With 20 kilometres to go, they are 1'45'' ahead of the chase group.

headline: Bisiaux reacts
subtext: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) accelerates. The strongest climbers from the chase group follow the French youngster, starting with his compatriot Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step).

headline: 15 kilometres to go
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Tobias Johannessen, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) are inside the last 2 kilometres of the penultimate climb.

headline: Van Aert leads the way to the summit
subtext: A little bit over a minute behind, Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step) has increased the pace at the front of the chase group.

headline: Results at Puerto de San Rafael (cat. 2, km 135.3)
subtext: 1. Van Aert, 5 pts 2. Lutsenko, 3 pts 3. Leknessund, 1 pt

headline: The final climb: Aramon Valdelinares!
subtext: The five leaders are oneminute ahead of the chasers at the bottom of the final climb: 9.8km at 5.9%. The gradients reach 13% on several ramps.

headline: Leknessund goes solo with 7.5 km to go
subtext: Lutsenko drives the chase with Johannessen on his wheel. Van Aert and Dunbar struggle.

headline: The peloton start the final climb
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) sets the pace. The gap at the bottom: 6'40''.

headline: 5 km to go for Leknessund
subtext: The Norwegian powerhouse is in pain, but he still has energy in his tank.

headline: Leknessund goes hard
subtext: The Norwegian is 3 km from the win. +40'' Van Aert, Johannessen +1'20'' Omrzel, JF Rodriguez, Sosa Meanwhile, Decathlon CMA CGM take the reins of the bunch.

headline: The GC group has exploded
subtext: Riccitello sets the pace, followed by Mühlberger, Gall, Pogacar, Mas, Roglic, Onley, Tejada, Kuss, Carapaz.

headline: Gall attacks
subtext: He is followed by Pogacar and Mas. Roglic and Onley are a few metres behind.

headline: Andreas Leknessund wins stage 7 of La Vuelta 2026
subtext: His team's first success in the Spanish Grand Tour... And it will be a 1-2 with Johannessen!

headline: Pogacar sets his own pace
subtext: Gall is a few metres behind, and then it's Mas.

headline: Top 5
subtext: 1. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) 2. Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility), +34'' 3. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), +47'' 4. Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), +58'' 5. Juan Felipe Rodriguez (EF Education-EasyPost), +1'13''

headline: Pogacar gains a handful of seconds
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) finishes 19th, with a gap of 4'23''. 20. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), +4'29'' 21. Enric Mas (Movistar), +4'39'' 22. Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), +4'52'' Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) finish with Kuss.

headline: Andreas Leknessund takes the win in Valdelinares
